scope: Proposition 15.1 (Strict rest reduction) of the manuscript “Spacetime Penrose inequalities: enclosing area, charge, and rigidity” (preprints/Spacetime-Penrose-inequalities-enclosing-area-charge-and-rigidity-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 794bf524061c4b36), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 98. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For a charged exterior as in Definition 14.1, E > |P| and m = (E2 − |P|2)1/2 > 0. There are smooth data (gj, Kj) on the same exterior, with the same flux forms, satisfying the following properties. (1) The physical matter condition is strict everywhere, the original boundary S has θ+,j < 0, and the constraint densities remain integrable. For one fixed 0 < δ < 1 the matter margin satisfies M0,j = 8π(µm,j − |Jm,j|gj ) ≥ cjr−3−δ y far out, cj > 0. (2) In a rest chart y, Kj is compactly supported and gj − δeucl = Ok(r−1 y ), Rgj = Ok(r−3−δ y ) for every k. The fields have the required O1(r−2 y ) decay. In particular the ADM momentum is zero and Ricgj = O(r−3 y ). (3) Smooth convergence holds on every compact set, including at S, and (15.1) Ej −→ m, agj (S) −→ ag(S), (QE,j, QB,j) = (QE, QB). Moreover gj ≥ (1 − εj)g globally for some εj ↓ 0.
